instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Dan 4:34 the reason is the faculty of a named person: Nebuchadnezzar speaks in the first person, and my reason is his own, the word that returns to him.
observations.grounds: my reason returned to me

observations.text: In Isa 1:18 the Lord is named as the speaker who calls the people to reason together with him: the reasoning is set between God and the people he addresses.
observations.grounds: let us reason together, says the Lord

observations.text: In Luk 9:47 Jesus is named as the one who knows the reasoning of others: the reasoning belongs to the disciples, referred to by their hearts, and Jesus is the knower of it.
observations.grounds: knowing the reasoning of their hearts

observations.text: In Act 19:8 and Act 19:9 the one reasoning is referred to by pronoun only (he), and those reasoned with are named by group: the synagogue, the disciples taken with him, the hall of Tyrannus; God is named in the kingdom of God, the subject of the reasoning. In 1Cor 13:11 the one who reasoned is I, the speaker who became a man.
observations.grounds: he withdrew from them and took the disciples with him

observations.text: Where the subgroup's word is a phrase of cause, God is named in the verse, not as the one who reasons: the Lord and God in Job 1:9, Jesus and God in Mar 12:24, Christ Jesus in Eph 3:1 (with I, Paul), Jesus Christ in 1Ti 1:16, God in 2Ti 1:6, Christ the Lord in 1Pe 3:15 (the data gives lord two codes, G2962 and G2316), the Son of God in 1Jo 3:8.
observations.grounds: the Son of God appeared

observations.text: Where the subgroup's word is a phrase of cause, people are named or referred to in the verse: Joshua and the men of war in Jos 5:4, Solomon and David in 1Ki 11:27 (the he who lifted his hand is not named in the verse), Job in Job 1:9, a man in Pro 3:30, the men Peter addresses in Act 10:21, the brothers in 1Th 3:7.
observations.grounds: this is the reason why Joshua circumcised them

observations.text: In Act 19:8 and Act 19:9 the reasoning runs outward from one person to others: he reasons with them in the synagogue, about the kingdom of God, and daily in the hall of Tyrannus with the disciples.
observations.grounds: reasoning and persuading them

observations.text: In Isa 1:18 the reasoning runs both ways: the Lord speaks and the verb is first person plural, let us, so the reasoning is held together between him and the people.
observations.grounds: let us reason together

observations.text: In Luk 9:47 and 1Cor 13:11 the reasoning is addressed to no one: it is held within, in their hearts, or by the speaker as a child. In Luk 9:47 Jesus' knowing runs toward that inner reasoning from outside it.
observations.grounds: knowing the reasoning of their hearts

observations.text: In Dan 4:34 the reason moves toward its owner: it returns to Nebuchadnezzar after he lifts his eyes to heaven.
observations.grounds: my reason returned to me

observations.text: In Act 10:21 and 1Pe 3:15 a reason is an account asked and given: Peter asks the men for the reason of their coming, and the believer gives a reason to anyone who asks; it runs from the one asked to the one asking.
observations.grounds: anyone who asks you for a reason

observations.text: In Job 1:9 and Pro 3:30 the cause is denied: fearing God and contending are said to have no ground behind them.
observations.grounds: for no reason

observations.text: Where the subgroup's word is a phrase of cause, it points from a ground to an act: to the circumcision in Jos 5:4, the raised hand in 1Ki 11:27, being wrong in Mar 12:24, Paul's prayer in Eph 3:1, being comforted in 1Th 3:7, the mercy received in 1Ti 1:16, the reminder in 2Ti 1:6, the appearing of the Son of God in 1Jo 3:8.
observations.grounds: For this reason I remind you

observations.text: In Dan 4:34 lifted (H5191) stands three words before reason: Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven and his reason returned, two clauses in sequence joined by and; the lifting comes first.
observations.grounds: lifted my eyes to heaven

observations.text: In Act 28:20 asked (G3870) stands two words after the phrase for this reason, which governs it: the cause comes first and the asking to see them follows from it.
observations.grounds: I have asked to see you

observations.text: In 1Pe 3:15 the reason (G3056) is what is asked for: asks (G0154) stands two words before it, and the one who asks seeks an account of the hope.
observations.grounds: anyone who asks you for a reason

observations.text: In Act 19:9 unbelief (G0544) stands ten words before reasoning: some continued in unbelief, and so he withdrew and took the disciples with him to reason elsewhere; the unbelief of the hearers is what moves the reasoning to the hall of Tyrannus.
observations.grounds: continued in unbelief

observations.text: In 1Th 3:5, 1Th 3:7 and 1Ti 1:16 the phrase for this reason points ahead to a clause whose object or means is faith: Paul sends to learn of their faith, their faith is the means of the comfort, and the mercy is shown as a pattern for future believers.
observations.grounds: through your faith

observations.text: In Pro 3:30 harm (H7451C) stands four words after for no reason, in the clause that gives the ground for it: the man has done no harm, so to contend with him is without cause.
observations.grounds: when he has done you no harm

observations.text: In Num 18:32 profane (H2490H) stands in the next sentence, not joined to by reason of it: the reason phrase frees the giver from sin, and the warning not to profane the holy things follows as its own command.
observations.grounds: you shall not profane the holy things

observations.text: In Dan 4:34 blessed (H1289) stands three words after reason, in the clause that follows its return: once his reason is back, the king blesses the Most High.
observations.grounds: and I blessed the Most High

observations.text: In Act 19:8 boldly (G3955) stands directly before reasoning: he spoke boldly, reasoning and persuading them, so the reasoning is part of the bold speaking in the synagogue.
observations.grounds: spoke boldly, reasoning and persuading them

observations.text: In Act 28:18 liberty (G0630G) stands three words before reason: the wish to release Paul rests on the absence of any cause for a death sentence.
observations.grounds: they wished to set me at liberty

observations.text: In Jam 3:17 pure (G0053) stands four places before open to reason in one list of the qualities of the wisdom from above: pure comes first, and open to reason follows after then, peaceable and gentle; they are joined only by the list.
observations.grounds: first pure, then peaceable

observations.text: In Jos 5:4 war (H4421) stands ten words after reason, in the explanation the reason introduces: the fighting men who left Egypt died on the way, and that is why Joshua circumcised the people.
observations.grounds: all the men of war, had died in the wilderness

observations.text: In 1Th 3:7 comforted (G3870) stands eight words after for this reason, which governs it: the cause comes first and being comforted about them follows from it.
observations.grounds: we have been comforted about you

observations.text: In 1Sa 20:29 commanded (H6680) stands nine words before for this reason, inside the excuse it sums up: the brother's command to be at the sacrifice is part of the cause given for the absence. The data holds a second code at the same place, H1931 (he), joined to the verb.
observations.grounds: my brother has commanded me to be there

observations.text: In Dan 4:34 praised (H7624) stands five words after reason, among the acts of worship that follow its return: blessing, praising and honoring the one who lives forever.
observations.grounds: praised and honored him

observations.text: In Jam 3:17 gentle (G1933) stands directly before open to reason, the next quality in the list of the wisdom from above.
observations.grounds: gentle, open to reason

observations.text: In 1Pe 3:15 gentleness (G4240) stands six words after reason and gives the manner of giving it: the defense for the hope is to be made with gentleness and respect.
observations.grounds: do it with gentleness and respect

observations.text: In 1Pe 3:15 always (G0104) stands seven words before reason and qualifies the readiness to give it: the believer is to be ready at all times with a defense for the hope.
observations.grounds: always being prepared to make a defense

observations.text: In Dan 4:34 and 1Ti 1:16 the words of lasting time qualify other nouns, not the reason: the everlasting dominion of God, and eternal life at the end of the purpose clause.
observations.grounds: for eternal life

observations.text: In Act 18:4 and Act 19:8 persuade (G3982) stands beside the reasoning (G1256), six and two words after it, joined by and: the reasoning and the persuading are one activity in the synagogue. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through argue, a synonym; the verses show the pairing with persuade instead.
observations.grounds: tried to persuade Jews and Greeks

observations.text: In Act 18:14 wrongdoing (G0092) and crime (G4467) stand in the condition before reason: Gallio would have a ground to hear the complaint only if a wrong or a crime were in question; the reason depends on the offence.
observations.grounds: a matter of wrongdoing or vicious crime

observations.text: In Gen 41:31 and Gen 47:13 severe (H3515) describes the famine that by reason of names as the cause: the severity of the famine is what makes it a cause, of plenty forgotten and of the land wasting.
observations.grounds: the famine was very severe

observations.text: In 1Sa 20:29 favor (H2580) stands five words before for this reason, inside the request it sums up: David asks leave on the condition of having found favor, and that request is the cause given for his absence.
observations.grounds: if I have found favor in your eyes

observations.text: In Act 24:25 will (G3333, summon) stands seventeen words after reasoned, in Felix's reply: the reasoning ends with Felix sending Paul away and promising to call him later; the words are not joined.
observations.grounds: I will summon you

observations.text: In Act 28:18 wished (G1014) stands four words before reason, and the reason clause gives its ground: the wish to free Paul rests on there being no cause for death.
observations.grounds: they wished to set me at liberty

observations.text: In 1Jo 3:8 destroy (G3089) stands five words after the reason, in the clause it introduces: the purpose of the appearing of the Son of God is the destroying of the devil's works.
observations.grounds: to destroy the works of the devil

observations.text: In Num 18:32 die (H4191) closes the warning of the next sentence, eight words after the reason phrase and not joined to it.
observations.grounds: lest you die

verses.text: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and sincere.
for this reason, brothers, in all our distress and affliction we have been comforted about you through your faith.
Do not contend with a man for no reason, when he has done you no harm.
For this reason I, Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles —
But I received mercy for this reason, that in me, as the foremost, Jesus Christ might display his perfect patience as an example to those who were to believe in him for eternal life.
but in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; yet do it with gentleness and respect,
Then Satan answered the Lord and said, “Does Job fear God for no reason?
And he entered the synagogue and for three months spoke boldly, reasoning and persuading them about the kingdom of God.
Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil.
And you shall bear no sin by reason of it, when you have contributed the best of it. But you shall not profane the holy things of the people of Israel, lest you die.’”
And this was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon built the Millo, and closed up the breach of the city of David his father.
Jesus said to them, “Is this not the reason you are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
And Peter went down to the men and said, “ I am the one you are looking for. What is the reason for your coming?”
But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “ If it were a matter of wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, I would have reason to accept your complaint.
And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix was alarmed and said, “ Go away for the present. When I get an opportunity I will summon you.”
For this reason, therefore, I have asked to see you and speak with you, since it is because of the hope of Israel that I am wearing this chain.”

He said, ‘Let me go, for our clan holds a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has commanded me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away and see my brothers.’ For this reason he has not come to the king’s table.”
“ Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
And this is the reason why Joshua circumcised them: all the males of the people who came out of Egypt, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way after they had come out of Egypt.
When they had examined me, they wished to set me at liberty, because there was no reason for the death penalty in my case.
and the plenty will be unknown in the land by reason of the famine that will follow, for it will be very severe.

But when some became stubborn and continued in unbelief, speaking evil of the Way before the congregation, he withdrew from them and took the disciples with him, reasoning daily in the hall of Tyrannus.
For this reason, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to learn about your faith, for fear that somehow the tempter had tempted you and our labor would be in vain.
For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands,
Now there was no food in all the land, for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished by reason of the famine.
But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts, took a child and put him by his side
When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I gave up childish ways.

At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and praised and honored him who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom endures from generation to generation;
And he reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and tried to persuade Jews and Greeks.
